summary: Steel lookout tower in Oregon County, Mark Twain NF: 100 ft, erected 1934; cabin, floor, picnic-ground and family-staffing notes 1936-1942; no status found.

events.note: Tower erected; the page describes a 100-foot steel tower.
Cabin being erected at the tower as living quarters for the lookout man, built by local ERA men with men working out of Camp F-17.
Tower refloored; plywood lining installed below the windows.
Work started on picnic grounds at the Braswell Lookout site.
Towerman Harley Dickerson, then at Eastwood, transferred back to the Braswell tower.
April 1942 item places Harvey Dickerson and his family at the Braswell Tower.

notes_for_editor: No source read gives status, access or a visit route, so the story says so. The 1936-1942 items come from a single hobbyist site quoting local newspapers (Shannon County Democrat, The Current Local); the newspapers themselves were not read. Two searches returned only directory pages (anyplaceamerica.com, mapcarta.com) listing a feature called Braswell Lookout Tower; they were not read or cited. Unread leads: the State Historical Society of Missouri 'Oregon County Place Names, 1928-1945' cited by Wikipedia, and Bob Frakes's book on Missouri lookout towers. Record height 30.5 m matches the 100-foot 1934 figure; no conflict found. Status stays unknown.
